findings.title: Unicode negation inside a quoted reminder title suppresses a supported positive task
findings.introduced_by: The sole task-compiler delta broadens _NEGATED to four Unicode apostrophes; compile_reminder_complete still applies it to raw text including quoted target data.
findings.trigger: Complete reminder called "Archive: don’t check this item"
findings.expected: Compile reminder.complete with target exactly Archive: don’t check this item; resolve the isolated matching reminder and issue one fake complete_reminder call with literal title and singular expected_id.
findings.actual: compile_task returns None. Actual main.agent executes zero calls, stores no task or workflow, and responds: I couldn't complete every requested step. Still missing one of: complete_reminder.
findings.variants: U+2019, U+2018, U+02BC, U+FF07, each with check and delete inside the quoted title: eight independent reproductions.
findings.isolation: On this same exact head, injecting only the previous ASCII _NEGATED regex in memory restores the exact literal target and expected fake completion call for all four Unicode forms. Four current-head ordinary Unicode names also complete the same fake call path. This is a one-line guard counterfactual, not execution or a pass claim at the old candidate.
findings.impact: Functional regression for the already-supported Complete reminder called grammar. No unauthorized effect or private read occurred in these controls.
findings.recommendation: Apply negation detection to quote-masked instruction text while retaining original quoted target bytes for parsing. Add positive quoted-negation target tests alongside real negative instruction and existing source-exclusion tests.
findings.ascii_limit: The analogous ASCII quoted-negation limitation predates this repair; the four newly covered Unicode forms are the demonstrated regression. The separately disclosed Check off reminder called observation is unchanged and not relied on.
